before.title: Autopilot/TACC Phantom Braking on Highway (NHTSA PE22-002, 416k Model 3/Y)
before.description: After Tesla moved to Vision-Only Autopilot in May 2021, 2021-2022 Model Y (and Model 3) owners reported hundreds of cases of the car suddenly applying brakes for no visible reason at highway speed while Autopilot or TACC is engaged. NHTSA's Office of Defects Investigation opened PE22-002 in February 2022 covering ~416,000 vehicles after initially 354 complaints, growing to 758+ by mid-2022 and 1,845+ (including 272 from 2023 models) in follow-up reporting.
before.solution: Keep firmware current; some owners report improvement on newer FSD builds. If recurrent, disable Autopilot/TACC in problem zones and file a complaint at nhtsa.gov so the open NHTSA investigation has data. No mechanical repair available.
symptoms: Sudden brake application on Autopilot or TACC
Forward Collision Warning with no visible obstacle
Rapid deceleration on highway
Often triggered near overpasses, shadows, or oncoming traffic
Repeated events in one drive

before.title: Battery Pack Contactor Opens Suddenly Causing Loss of Drive Power (Recall 25V690 / SB-25-13-001)
before.description: On 2026 Model Y (built ~Mar 15 to Aug 15, 2025) and 2025 Model 3 vehicles, a battery pack contactor can open unexpectedly because of a poor coil-termination connection in the contactor's solenoid. When it opens, the flow of electricity from the high-voltage battery to the drive motor(s) stops, causing a sudden loss of propulsion with no advance warning; the screen then instructs the driver to pull over safely. The contactor solenoid was supplied by a third party (Sistemas Mecatronicos/InTiCa) and built into SongChuan contactors. Tesla identified 36 warranty claims and 26 field reports. The recall covers 12,963 vehicles, of which roughly 7,925 are 2026 Model Y.
before.solution: This is a hardware defect that cannot be fixed over-the-air. Affected owners must take the vehicle to a Tesla Service Center, where technicians replace the battery pack contactors free of charge under warranty.
symptoms: Sudden loss of drive power / loss of propulsion while driving
'Pull over safely' or vehicle-needs-service warning on screen
Car coasts to a stop with no prior warning
Vehicle will not move / no drive after contactor opens

before.title: Electronic Door Handles Inoperative on Low 12V Voltage — Occupants Trapped (NHTSA Investigation PE25-010)
before.description: NHTSA opened Preliminary Evaluation PE25010 on September 15, 2025, covering an estimated 174,290 2021 Model Y vehicles after at least 9 to 16 reports that the exterior electronic door handles became inoperative when the car's low-voltage (12V) system dropped to insufficient voltage. The electronic releases (both exterior and, for occupants who can't reach them, interior) stop working, so doors cannot be opened. Several complaints involve parents who had just placed or retrieved children in the rear seats; in four of nine documented cases the parents broke windows to get back in. No low-voltage battery warning appeared before the handles failed. The probe lists 2017-2022 Model 3 and Model Y as peer vehicles and was reported to be widening in late 2025.
before.solution: No recall remedy has been issued yet (investigation open as of late 2025). Tesla vehicles have manual interior door release levers; owners and passengers should learn the manual-release location for every door (front doors have an obvious mechanical pull; rear doors on Model Y have a hidden manual release). Keeping the 12V/low-voltage battery healthy and replacing it promptly when it weakens reduces the risk. Owners experiencing a dead 12V condition can use the exterior emergency low-voltage terminals to power the front trunk and access the cabin.
symptoms: Exterior door handle does nothing when pressed
Doors will not unlock or open with no prior warning
Occupants (especially children) trapped inside
Total loss of electronic door release tied to low 12V battery voltage

before.title: Electronic Power Steering Assist Loss From Overstressed Circuit Board (Recall 25V092 / SB-25-00-004)
before.description: On 2023 Model 3 and Model Y vehicles built roughly Feb 28 to Oct 11, 2023, running software prior to 2023.38.4, the printed circuit board for the electronic power steering assist can experience an overstress condition. This causes a loss of power steering assist when the vehicle comes to a stop and then accelerates again, requiring much greater steering effort, especially at low speeds. The defect followed a lengthy NHTSA investigation (PE23-016, later upgraded to an engineering analysis) that collected more than 2,300 complaints alleging loss of steering or steering control, including at least one crash. Tesla recalled 376,241 Model 3 and Model Y vehicles in February 2025.
before.solution: Tesla issued a free over-the-air software update (2023.38.4 or later) that revises the power-up sequence and current handling to prevent the EPS circuit board from being overstressed. No service-center visit is required; owners simply need to ensure the vehicle is updated. Vehicles that already suffered a hardware failure of the steering board are repaired under warranty.
symptoms: Steering wheel becomes very hard to turn after stopping and accelerating again
Power steering assist fault / 'Steering assist reduced' warning on screen
Heavy steering effort at low speeds and in parking maneuvers
Loss of steering control warning message

before.title: Front Suspension Lateral Link Bolts Loose - Separation Risk (Recall 21V-835)
before.description: On 2020-2021 Model Y built March 2020-June 2021, the two fasteners connecting the front lower control arm (lateral link) to the subframe were not torqued to spec at the factory. The bolts can back out over time, allowing the lateral link to separate from the subframe and causing sudden loss of wheel alignment and steering control. NHTSA Recall 21V-835 / Tesla SB-21-31-003 covers inspection and re-torque.
before.solution: Check VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls for open 21V-835 status. Tesla Service inspects and re-torques (or replaces) the lateral link fasteners free of charge. Do not delay - this is a separation-risk recall.
symptoms: Clunking from front suspension over bumps
Wandering steering
Uneven tire wear
Visible loose or missing bolt at subframe
Sudden alignment shift after pothole

before.title: Heat Pump / Octovalve Failure in Cold Weather (Loss of Cabin Heat and Defrost)
before.description: On 2021-2022 Model Y, the heat pump's Electronic Expansion Valve (EXV) in the Octovalve supermanifold can stick open if controller communication is interrupted, causing total loss of cabin heat and defrost in sub-freezing temperatures (especially -10C/14F or colder). In severe cases the AC compressor and Octovalve must be replaced. Tesla recalled ~26,681 vehicles (NHTSA 22V-050, Feb 2022) across Model S/X/3/Y running firmware 2021.44 through 2021.44.30.6 for the software-related issue, but hardware failures also occur, especially in extreme cold.
before.solution: Update firmware to 2021.44.30.7 or later per NHTSA recall 22V-050. If heat is still lost, request Tesla Service inspect the Octovalve and AC compressor; warranty covers replacement on most 2021-2022 vehicles.
symptoms: No cabin heat
Windshield will not defrost
HVAC blows cold air only
Heat pump runs but no warmth
Warning message about climate system

before.title: Liftgate Water Ingress Into Trunk and Subtrunk (Service Bulletin SB-23-10-003)
before.description: 2020-2023 Model Y crossovers built at Fremont and Giga Austin can leak water into the rear trunk and subtrunk through gaps around the liftgate lamp studs and connector, and through inadequate liftgate sealing. Owners report standing water in the spare-tire well, soaked carpet, and water cascading out when the trunk is opened after rain. Tesla released SB-23-10-003 (April 2023) to reseal the assembly.
before.solution: Request service under TSB SB-23-10-003. Tesla replaces the liftgate lamp double-ended stud gaskets and connector gaskets and applies polymer sealant (about 1.8 hours of labor, covered for many owners). Dry the subtrunk fully first to prevent mold.
symptoms: Water pooling in subtrunk / spare-tire well
Wet trunk carpet after rain or car wash
Water streaming out when opening the liftgate
Musty smell from rear of cabin
Corrosion on trunk-mounted electronics

before.title: Premature Rear Tire Wear From Aggressive Negative Camber
before.description: 2020-2024 Model Y (especially Performance trim, which sits ~10mm lower) is delivered with aggressive, non-adjustable rear negative camber that causes severe inner-edge wear on the rear tires. The factory rear camber cannot be changed via standard alignment — only toe is adjustable. Owners commonly replace rear tires every 15-25k miles, with some Performance owners going through 3 sets in 60k miles. The 400+ lb-ft of instant rear-wheel torque combined with the vehicle's 4,400-4,600 lb weight amplifies the wear.
before.solution: Get a four-wheel alignment at first sign of inner wear. For lasting fix, install adjustable rear camber arms (N2itive, MPP, Unplugged Performance) and re-align to about -1.0deg camber with neutral toe. Rotate tires every 5-6k miles thereafter.
symptoms: Smooth/balding inner shoulder of rear tires while outer is fine
Cords or wear bars showing on inner edge under 25k miles
Cupping or feathering on inner rear tread
Pull or off-center steering wheel from delivery

before.title: Rearview/Backup Camera Image Loss From Shorted Computer Circuit Board (Recall 25V002 / SB-25-00-001)
before.description: On certain 2023-2025 Model Y (and 2023-2025 Model X, 2024-2025 Model 3/S) vehicles, the vehicle's computer (infotainment/MCU) circuit board can short due to a reverse-current condition on startup. When this happens, the rearview camera image fails to appear when the driver shifts into reverse, leaving a blank screen and forcing reliance on mirrors and shoulder checks — a violation of FMVSS 111 rear-visibility requirements. Tesla discovered the issue in November 2024 after a rising number of warranty computer replacements for shorted boards. The recall covers more than 239,000 vehicles.
before.solution: Tesla released free over-the-air software updates (versions 2024.44.25.3 and 2024.45.25.6 or later) that change the power-up sequence to prevent the circuit board / power components from shorting. Any vehicle whose computer already shorted before the update is given a free replacement computer under warranty.
symptoms: Blank/black rearview camera screen when shifting into reverse
Backup camera not displaying image
Center touchscreen or computer behaving abnormally before failure
Increased warranty computer (MCU) replacements

before.title: Refreshed (Juniper) Model Y Turn-Signal Stalk Fails to Latch / Cancels Early
before.description: The 2025-2026 'Juniper' refresh re-added a physical turn-signal stalk after the steering-wheel haptic buttons proved unpopular, but owners report the new stalk is unreliable. It frequently will not 'hold' a continuous signal — many drivers report only about three blink cycles before it cancels, requiring repeated re-pressing or holding the stalk through a turn. The stalk lacks the traditional detented second click that latches the signal on, and owners on Tesla forums describe it as flimsy/cheap-feeling and counter-intuitive, a genuine safety annoyance because signals stop mid-maneuver. This is a design/usability defect rather than a recall.
before.solution: No official recall or fix. Tesla has adjusted behavior through software in some builds; a firm but quick flick is reported to latch it more reliably. Owners frustrated with the operation can raise a service ticket, though Tesla generally treats this as designed behavior. Aftermarket stalk-feel guides and software updates may improve reliability over time.
symptoms: Turn signal cancels after only a few blinks
Stalk will not hold a continuous signal during a turn
Driver must hold or repeatedly press the stalk
Stalk feels flimsy or cheap

before.title: Model S / Model X First-Row Seat Belt Anchor Inspection Recall (23V-488)
before.description: NHTSA recall 23V-488 covers approximately 15,869 Tesla Model S (2021-2023) and Model X (2021-2023) vehicles for first-row seat belts that may not have been properly reconnected to their pretensioner anchors after a prior repair. If the anchor connection is below spec, the seat belt may not restrain the occupant correctly in a crash. (Note: this entry was originally drafted as a Model Y recall during the EV batch; the actual recall affects S/X, not Y — listing under Model Y for legacy slug reasons but the affected vehicles are S/X 2021-2023.)
before.solution: Free recall remedy at any Tesla service center — inspection and, if needed, reconnection or full seatbelt assembly replacement. Check VIN against 23V-488. Tesla has not reported crashes or injuries linked to this defect.
symptoms: loose seatbelt anchor
safety recall

before.title: Sentry Mode and Cabin Overheat Protection Excessive Battery Drain (12V and HV)
before.description: Leaving Sentry Mode and/or Cabin Overheat Protection enabled on 2020-2024 Model Y causes 7-14% HV pack drain per day plus accelerated 12V battery cycling, because the car keeps the HV system live, cameras recording, and the Autopilot computer processing video continuously. Owners report dead 12V batteries, range anxiety, and inability to drive after a few unplugged days. Tesla added throttling in 2024.32.6 and a ~40% reduction in 2024.38.4, but baseline drain remains substantial.
before.solution: Update to 2024.38.4 or later (40% drain reduction via FSD-computer motion detection offload; MCU stays asleep until video write). Use 2024.32.6+ behavior that cuts 12V outlets/USB in Sentry. Disable Sentry Mode and Cabin Overheat Protection during long-term parking, or whitelist home/work. Replace the 12V battery if drain persists: 2020-2021 and early 2022 builds are flooded lead-acid; production starting late December 2021 transitioned to a 15.5V Li-ion module — do NOT cross-fit the wrong chemistry.
symptoms: Phantom drain of 5-15% per day when parked
12V battery dead after several unplugged days
Premature 12V battery replacement (often <2 years on early lead-acid units)
'Vehicle may not restart' / 'Power reduced' 12V low warnings
Car cannot wake or shift to Drive after parking

before.title: TPMS Warning Light Resets Between Drives, Failing to Warn of Low Tire Pressure (Recall 24V935)
before.description: Software release 2024.38.3 introduced a defect on 2020-2025 Model Y (and 2017-2025 Model 3, 2024 Cybertruck) vehicles in which the tire pressure monitoring system warning telltale would reset when the vehicle was powered down or went to sleep between drives. As a result, the low-tire-pressure warning light did not remain illuminated across drive cycles as required by FMVSS 138, so a driver could begin a new trip unaware that a tire was still under-inflated. The recall covers approximately 694,000 vehicles.
before.solution: Tesla pushed a free over-the-air firmware update (release 2024.38.7, 2024.38.10, 2024.40 or later, excluding 2024.44/2024.44.1) that restores compliant TPMS telltale behavior so the warning persists between drives. No service visit is needed.
symptoms: Low tire pressure warning light disappears after the car sleeps or powers down
TPMS telltale not illuminated at start of a new drive despite low pressure
No persistent under-inflation warning between trips

before.title: Windshield Cracking During Cabin Preconditioning / Defrost in Cold Weather
before.description: Multiple Model Y owners report the windshield spontaneously cracking while using cabin preconditioning or the defrost function in cold weather. Owners describe a consistent crack pattern that appears as the heating system warms the cold glass, suggesting thermal stress on the windshield (sometimes attributed to the defrost/heating airflow and the heated-glass or windshield design). Because Tesla windshields are large, curved, and expensive, and the cracks are not the result of road debris, owners frequently dispute warranty coverage. This is an owner-documented pattern rather than a formal recall.
before.solution: Owners are advised to warm the cabin gradually rather than blasting maximum defrost onto very cold glass, and to clear ice mechanically before applying heat. If a crack appears without an impact point during preconditioning, document it and pursue a warranty/goodwill claim, though approval varies. Windshield replacement is the remedy if the glass cracks.
symptoms: Windshield cracks while using cabin preconditioning or defrost
Crack appears with no impact/chip point
Consistent crack pattern reported by multiple owners
Cracking onset in cold-weather warm-up
